---
title: "About Sailing in Unnecessary Detail"
---

This is a notebook about sailing, fluid dynamics and making sense of simulations.

The aim is to connect a sailor?s questions with pictures, calculations and explanations that can be read in a browser. Equations are part of the story; you should not need to download a paper to follow it.

The first articles explore an idealised sailboat sailing upwind. Later notes may cover interactions between boats, sail forces and how those forces relate to speed.

## Reading the results

Simulation results are estimates within a model. Each article explains its assumptions and distinguishes calculated quantities from further approximations. A colourful flow field is a starting point for questions, rather than proof that the model describes a real boat accurately.

## Figures and equations

Figures open at a larger size when clicked. SVG downloads retain sharp labels, outlines and contours. Dense colour fields may be embedded as images inside the SVG to keep loading times reasonable.

The site is written in Quarto and published from [its GitHub repository](https://github.com/chlyhne/sailing-in-unnecessary-detail).
